findings.reason: The protected Python solution determines if any two strings of equal width differ by exactly one character (Hamming distance 1). It computes double polynomial rolling hashes for all words, then iterates column by column. For each column index, it masks out the character at that position in O(1) time using precomputed positional powers and checks for matching signatures, validating matching prefix/suffix substrings to avoid hash collisions. Processing column-wise limits space usage to O(q + ell) space while running in expected O(q * ell) time. The implementation is expert quality; no candidate is required.

Double rolling hashes (moduli 10^9+7 and 10^9+9) minimize collision risk, and exact substring validation (prefix and suffix comparison) guarantees zero false positives. Column-wise iteration ensures matching masked signatures correspond to strings differing at the exact same index.

Computing initial double rolling hashes takes O(q * ell) time. Column-wise masking and hash set lookups take expected O(q * ell) time. Space complexity is O(q + ell) for hash arrays and column map. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts dict list of q equal-length strings, returning true if Hamming distance 1 pair exists and false otherwise.

The approach accurately details double polynomial rolling hash masking, column-by-column processing to manage memory, exact substring verification, and O(q * ell) time / O(q + ell) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover prefix/suffix trie-state identifiers, wildcard string materialization overhead, all-pairs comparison quadratic costs, width-1 strings, boundary character differences, two-difference rejection, distinct string invariants, column identity matching, and single-word inputs.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical double-hash column-wise masking algorithm with SHA-256 digests 1c1b82ab0b12bd869b2b622a7ea996a9ec78fb0f5b6788fd1b25c1ff72d82103 and b1fe61dc3b86395ae860741c0acba14240ef5f9c22692e51ae7b070ce95924c0.
